blockingFindings: persistCodexAppReviewResult writes the successful run envelope and review result through separate non-atomic writes, while persistReviewResult writes directly to the final path. Interruption can leave successful provenance without a valid review artifact or leave a partial result. Use staged validated output with atomic publication and cleanup on failure.
missingNegativeTests: Simulate interruption or write failure between Codex-app run-envelope publication and review-result publication, including partial-result recovery.

architectureAssessment.deepModules: The launcher separates routing, parsing, cancellation, validation, lifecycle binding, and persistence into bounded helpers, though persistence paths should share one atomic publication primitive.
architectureAssessment.hexagonalArchitecture: Process execution, filesystem evidence, and review assessment binding are explicit adapters around governed validation logic; Codex-app persistence currently bypasses the safer staged publication path.
architectureAssessment.eventedBoundaries: Structured progress and terminal events clearly separate launch, child output, cancellation, failure, and successful review binding.

exactNextAction: Revise only Codex-app and shared review-result persistence to use validated staging and atomic final publication, then rerun the packet-required deterministic checks and resubmit semanticReview on the same governed scope.
